Our Values
At Nightingale, we aim:
To create a happy, safe, caring and disciplined environment, maximising the children's opportunity to develop and learn
To encourage each child to realize his/her full potential through active involvement in their own learning, valuing the varied experiences that each child brings to school
To encourage active participation of parents/carers in all aspects of school life
To develop the whole child - socially, emotionally and physically as well as academically
To maintain a supportive framework where all members of the school community feel valued, secure, confident and positive about their role
To provide a broad, balanced, coherent, differentiated and relevant education for all children
Our values are embedded in all that we do. They are the thread that holds us together.
Our values are:
images

British Values
text
The DfE have stated that schools should actively promote “the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
As a result of the promotion of British values, pupils at Nightingale are expected to develop:
An understanding of how citizens can influence decision-making through the democratic process;
An appreciation that living under the rule of law protects individual citizens and is essential for their wellbeing and safety;
An understanding that there is a separation of power between the executive and the judiciary, and that whilst some public bodies such as the police and the army can be held to account through Parliament, others such as the courts maintain independence;
An understanding that the freedom to choose and hold other faiths and beliefs is protected in law;
An acceptance that other people having different faiths and beliefs to oneself (or having none) should be accepted and tolerated, and should not be the cause of prejudicial or discriminatory behaviour.
An understanding of the importance of identifying and combatting discrimination.
At Nightingale, British Values are promoted through a variety of channels, such as:
Stonewall Education Champions Initiative
Teaching within the curriculum
Planned assembly themes
The promotion of our school Vision and Ethos
The implementation of our school behaviour policy and inclusion policy
Use of rewards and sanctions
Extended curriculum e.g. trips, visitors and themed weeks
Celebration of work through displays, website, assembly
Provision of time for reflection and debate e.g. circle-time
This list is not exhaustive.
For more information, view Dfe Guidance for Promoting Fundamental British Values through SMSC

Our Aims
Text
Our goal is simple; it is to ensure that all children reach their full potential and develop their areas of interest and talent.
At Nightingale, we aim:
To support each child to become a positive role model and an excellent student
To provide all children with a broad and balanced curriculum that promotes and celebrates our differences
To create and maintain an environment where children and adults are able to learn, feel safe and cared for
To welcome and encourage participation from families and other members of the community
to realise their potential through active involvement in their own learning
To be a centre of support where all members of the school community feel valued, secure and confident
We seek to achieve our aims by:
Providing teaching that is of the highest quality
Providing learners with feedback that enables them to make greater progress
Providing all with a rich and varied curriculum
Welcoming and encouraging participation from all school stakeholders to support us in our continued drive to raise standards
Providing an environment where children’s safety and welfare are paramount
Maintaining an inclusive setting where all make progress, feel safe and are valued
Constantly striving to improve to ensure that our setting reflects the highest standards in education
Pupils will work towards these aims by:
Working hard to achieve our best in all aspects of school life
Having pride in our learning and showing it in assemblies
Making a positive contribution to the life of the school
Believing in ourselves and learning about each other
Showing respect for each other, for adults in the school and for the environment
Treating others how we would like to be treated
Staff will work towards these aims by:
Creating a stimulating, well organised and high-quality environment that enhances teaching and learning, and motivates pupils
Planning and implementing the full range of national curriculum subjects (including Religious Education) and the Early Learning Goals
Planning thoroughly to match learning to pupils needs and to extend and challenge them using regular assessment of pupil progress to establish pupils current achievements, and set targets for future development
Having high expectations of oneself as a teacher and being committed to one’s own professional development
Being sensitive and aware of pupils’ cultures, religions and backgrounds
Welcoming parents to work in partnership with the school
Listening to the views and opinions of pupils
Parents will work towards these aims by:
Supporting the ethos and aims of Nightingale Primary School
Sharing responsibility for the learning of their children
Helping their children to understand school rules and their responsibility within them
Ensuring good punctuality and attendance of their children
Attending parent evenings and other functions
Support children with their homework
Being respectful to staff pupils and parents
Engaging in the life of the school
Local Academy Councillors will work towards these aims by:
Working in partnership with staff, pupils and their parents to decide upon and support the aims and values of the school
Supporting initiatives that ensure our pupils reach their full potential
Work alongside staff in a supportive manner
Engaging in the life of the school
Take responsibility for one’s own development and training as a governor
Carrying out monitoring and support roles where appropriate
Welcoming parents to work in partnership with the school

pageCache.pageTitle: Meet Our People - Nightingale Primary School
pageCache.text:
Meet Our People
text
The best way to understand what it's like to work at Nightingale Primary School is to hear from the people who make our school such a welcoming and supportive place every day.
Behind every success at Nightingale are the people who make our school what it is. From colleagues who have been part of the school community for decades to those beginning their education journey, every member of our team brings something unique.
Many members of staff have built long and rewarding careers at Nightingale, reflecting the strong relationships, supportive culture and sense of belonging that make our school such a special place to work. Others have joined more recently, bringing fresh ideas while quickly becoming part of our close-knit community.
If you're considering joining us, we hope these stories give you a genuine insight into what life at Nightingale is really like.
Real Staff Stories
Every colleague's journey is different, but there are common themes you'll hear throughout our school—supportive leadership, friendly colleagues, strong relationships with children and families, and the opportunity to make a real difference every single day.
Here's what some of our staff say about working at Nightingale Primary School.
‘The warm, almost family-like atmosphere between staff and children and amongst staff members. Staff trust and support each other and treat each other with respect and appreciation.’
‘The small size of the school. Flexibility with time changes and understanding with needing time off occasionally for parental responsibilities.’
‘School: Strong connection and bonds between staff, pupils and families. It is a wonderful community. ‘
‘I feel that the we all work as a team to improve the life chances of every student, and that shared mission creates a positive, collaborative atmosphere among staff. ‘
expander
The Difference Our People Make
Every member of staff plays an important role in making Nightingale Primary School the welcoming, inclusive community that it is.
Whether they're inspiring children in the classroom, supporting pupils to overcome challenges, working alongside families, leading enrichment opportunities or helping to strengthen our links with the local community, every colleague contributes to our shared vision of helping children flourish.
Together, we create a school where kindness, respect and ambition are part of everyday life, where diversity is celebrated, and where every child is encouraged to believe in themselves and achieve their potential.
It's the dedication, compassion and teamwork of our people that make Nightingale such a rewarding place to work and such a special place for children to learn.
Take the Next Step in Your Journey
If the stories on this page have inspired you, we'd love to hear from you.
At Nightingale Primary School, you'll become part of a caring, supportive team where your contribution is valued, your professional development is encouraged and every day offers the opportunity to make a lasting difference for children and families.
Explore our current opportunities or join our Talent Community to hear about future vacancies and become part of the Nightingale community.
View Vacancies | Join Our Talent Community

Part of Maritime Academy Trust
Text
Nightingale Primary School is proud to be part of Maritime Academy Trust—a family of schools working together to improve life chances for children and create meaningful career opportunities for the people who work within them.
Being part of the Trust means you're supported not only within our school, but also through a wider network of colleagues, expertise and opportunities that help you learn, grow and develop throughout your career.
What This Means For Your Career
At Nightingale, you will experience the close relationships and community spirit of a small school, while benefiting from the wider opportunities available through Maritime Academy Trust.
Opportunities to collaborate with and learn from colleagues across multiple schools
Access to high-quality professional learning and specialist training
Clear career pathways across teaching, leadership and professional services roles
Opportunities to contribute to Trust-wide projects and school improvement initiatives
Support from experienced colleagues and leaders across Maritime Academy Trust
A collaborative culture that encourages continuous learning, shared expertise and professional growth
Being part of the Trust means your opportunities extend beyond a single school, giving you access to a wide range of experiences, professional networks and future career opportunities.
A Close-Knit Community, A World of Opportunity
At Nightingale Primary School, you'll enjoy the benefits of working in a small, welcoming school where every colleague is known, relationships matter and community is at the heart of everything we do.
Our strong partnerships with families, commitment to inclusion and deep roots within the Woolwich community create a rewarding environment where staff can make a genuine difference every day while feeling supported as part of a close-knit team.
Alongside this, being part of Maritime Academy Trust opens the door to wider professional networks, specialist expertise and career development opportunities across a family of schools.
Together, this gives you the best of both worlds—the warmth, familiarity and sense of belonging of a community school, combined with the opportunities, collaboration and career progression that come from being part of a forward-thinking multi-academy trust.
Explore Opportunities Across Maritime Academy Trust
Whether you're exploring future career pathways, looking to develop new skills or considering your next opportunity, Maritime Academy Trust offers a wide range of support, development and progression opportunities.

Sports and Clubs
text
At Nightingale we run a number of sports, music, drama and other extra-curricular clubs for children in different year groups at different times during the academic year. Letters will be sent to notify you of these as they are arranged.
The clubs broaden the children's horizons and encourage them to consider interests they might not have otherwise thought of. This is reinforced by the regular demonstrations of the clubs for the rest of the school in our assemblies, which also provides an opportunity to celebrate the children's achievements.
After School Clubs are on offer during term time only. Please enquire at the School Office for further details.

SEND Local Offer
text
All Greenwich maintained schools have a similar approach to meeting the needs of pupils with Special Educational Needs and are supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress in school. All schools are supported to be as inclusive as possible, with the needs of pupils with Special Educational Need(s) being met in a mainstream setting wherever possible, where families want this to happen. Click on the link below to gain further detailed information about provision available for children with Special Educational Needs (SEN) and/or disabilities at Nightingale Primary School.
Full Details of our Local Offer
SEND policy & Information Report
To visit Greenwich Council's Local Offer site, please click here
Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo)
Mrs. Rantell is employed for 5 days a week as our school SENCo and achieved her qualification in November 2013. In her role, she meets with class teachers and teaching assistants to ensure all children are provided with appropriate support according to their need. She also line manages our speech and language therapists and liaises with other professionals to ensure we are effective in meeting the needs of our vulnerable children.
For more SEND information, please contact Mrs. Rantell through the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: English at Nightingale - Nightingale Primary School
pageCache.text:
English at Nightingale
text
Our Approach to Literacy at Nightingale Primary School
At Nightingale, we take an evidence-based, thematic approach to literacy, ensuring a well-rounded education for all our pupils. Each term, our learning centres around a core text, which serves as the foundation for developing key reading and writing skills. By incorporating metacognitive strategies like Making Thinking Visible (MTV) and collaborative learning methods such as Kagan Structures, we foster deeper comprehension and engagement across all areas of literacy.
expanders
Writing
We view writing as a multi-step process, enabling pupils to refine their skills at every stage:
Planning – Setting goals and generating ideas before beginning a piece of writing.
Drafting – Focusing on capturing key ideas.
Sharing – Encouraging pupils to share their work and receive feedback throughout the process.
Evaluating – Ensuring that writing goals are being met through regular reflection.
Revising – Making content improvements based on feedback and self-evaluation.
Editing – Ensuring the text is accurate and coherent.
Publishing – Presenting polished work for others to read.
Reading
Our daily reading sessions incorporate metacognitive strategies that enhance comprehension and engagement. Pupils develop an understanding of key reading domains by exploring:
What the reading domain is,
Why and when it is used.
Through Guided Oral Reading, teachers model fluent reading, while pupils practice and receive constructive feedback. Repeated Reading strategies allow pupils to re-read passages until they achieve fluency, ensuring mastery of complex texts.
Vocabulary Instruction
Building vocabulary is essential for reading comprehension and application in new contexts. We focus on:
Teaching 3-5 key Tier Two words weekly.
Using Dual Coding to reinforce connections between words and images.
Exploring synonyms, antonyms, and sentence structures through interactive activities such as chanting and cloze tasks.
Sentence Instruction
We enhance sentence construction through activities like sentence combining, helping pupils develop more complex, multi-clause sentences. Our approach includes:
Explicit instruction focusing on grammar and sentence mastery.
Modelling – "I do it"
Guided Practice – "We do it"
Check Understanding – "You do it"
By embedding grammar within writing tasks, we aim to improve both composition skills and overall content understanding.
Nightingale Reading Principles
An instructional strategy in which pupils read the same text multiple times increases fluency, comprehension, and vocabulary retention. This method also boosts confidence and self-esteem as pupils grow more adept at transferring their learning across texts.
A systematic approach to breaking down complex passages, asking text-dependent questions, and encouraging mastery through writing. Both repeated and close reading form the foundation of our reading instruction at Nightingale.
Fluency
Fluency is key to reading success. We use Repeated Reading techniques to ensure pupils develop automaticity—reading quickly and accurately. This leads to improved comprehension and a smoother transition between texts.
Early Reading
Our phonics programme, Nightingale Letters and Sounds, ensures all pupils progress from decoding words to reading fluently. Paired with decodable Big Cat Books, this provides a secure foundation for every child’s reading journey.
Accelerated Reader
This computer-based programme helps us monitor pupils' reading progress and guide them to books appropriate for their individual reading levels. Through daily reading and regular quizzes, children develop both pleasure in reading and comprehension skills.
MyOn
myON is a personalised digital library offering unlimited access to books tailored to each pupil's reading ability. This platform works in harmony with Star Reading and Accelerated Reader, enhancing literacy development both in school and at home.
Read Live Repeated Reading
The Read Naturally Strategy integrates teacher modelling, repeated reading, and progress monitoring to improve fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension. Using high-interest materials at individual skill levels, pupils track their progress and receive personalised instruction.
Reading Recovery
We use the Fischer Family Trust (FFT) Wave 3 programme as an early intervention for Year 1 pupils who face challenges in learning to read and write. Based on the principles of Reading Recovery, this programme helps pupils who require extra support but do not need full Reading Recovery intervention.
Nuffield Early Language Intervention
Our Nuffield Early Language Intervention (NELI) programme targets vocabulary, listening skills, and phonological awareness in pupils aged 4-5. Delivered by trained teaching assistants, this 20-week programme is proven to help children overcome language difficulties.
To learn more about how we assess pupil progress and implement teaching strategies in reading, writing, phonics, and language development, click below to explore our gradual release model and suggested teaching sequences.
Gradual release model and suggested teaching sequences
text
At Nightingale, we believe that strong literacy skills open doors for every child.
Our English curriculum is carefully planned, evidence-informed and centred around high-quality texts, rich talk and purposeful writing.
Each term, learning is built around a core text. These texts provide meaningful opportunities for children to develop their reading, writing, vocabulary, grammar, spoken language and wider understanding of the world.
Through our thematic approach, pupils are encouraged to make connections between subjects, explore important ideas and develop a love of reading and writing.
We use a range of research-informed strategies to support pupils’ learning, including:
activating prior knowledge;
explicit strategy instruction;
modelling of learned strategies;
memorisation of strategies and language structures;
independent practice;
structured reflection.
This gradual release approach helps pupils move from adult modelling and shared practice towards confident, independent application.
At Nightingale, this is particularly important because many of our pupils benefit from carefully structured talk, vocabulary development and repeated opportunities to rehearse language before writing.
expanders
Spoken Language, Oral Rehearsal and Writing
At Nightingale, we know that children need to say it before they can write it.
Oral rehearsal is central to our approach to English. Pupils are given regular opportunities to practise sentences aloud, rehearse ideas with a partner and refine their language before committing their writing to paper.
This supports pupils to organise their thoughts, develop vocabulary and build confidence with sentence structure.
Oral rehearsal is especially important for pupils who are developing confidence with spoken language, pupils with English as an additional language and pupils who may have strong ideas but find the written process challenging.
Teachers model high-quality spoken sentences and support pupils to improve them through questioning, recasting, partner talk and shared rehearsal.
Pupils are encouraged to listen to how a sentence sounds, improve it orally and then write it with greater confidence.
This helps children:
improve sentence accuracy;
organise their thinking;
reduce cognitive load;
speak with confidence;
write with greater clarity and control.
Oral rehearsal is not an additional activity at Nightingale. It is part of the writing process.
DRDR: Discuss, Rehearse, Draft and Redraft
At Nightingale, DRDR is a writing approach.
DiscussRehearseDraftRedraft
The approach supports pupils to develop writing sentence by sentence. Rather than expecting children to hold a whole paragraph or extended piece in their working memory, pupils are guided to focus carefully on one sentence at a time.
This reduces issues linked to executive function, working memory and cognitive overload.
Through DRDR, pupils discuss the idea first, rehearse the sentence orally, draft it, then redraft it until they own the sentence.
This means pupils are not simply copying or filling space. They are learning how to think like writers, shape language and improve their own work.
A typical DRDR sequence might include:
DiscussPupils talk through the idea, purpose, vocabulary and meaning of the sentence.
RehearsePupils say the sentence aloud, often more than once, improving it before writing.
DraftPupils write the sentence, focusing on accuracy, meaning and structure.
RedraftPupils improve the sentence by refining vocabulary, grammar, punctuation or impact.
This process is repeated sentence by sentence.
As pupils become more familiar with the routine, they build stamina and independence. They move from owning one sentence, to writing several connected sentences, and then to producing more extended pieces with greater control.
DRDR supports pupils to:
write with confidence;
reduce the pressure of holding too much information at once;
develop stronger sentence control;
rehearse vocabulary before writing;
understand how redrafting improves quality;
build independence over time.
At Nightingale, DRDR is particularly powerful because it gives all pupils a clear route into writing. It helps children who may struggle to begin, pupils who need language rehearsal and pupils who benefit from a structured routine.
Key Stage 1 Talk for Writing
In Key Stage 1, Talk for Writing plays an important role in helping children become confident early writers.
Children learn stories and text structures orally before they are expected to write independently.
This helps them internalise the rhythm, vocabulary and structure of different types of writing.
Through imitation, innovation and independent application, pupils learn how stories and sentences work.
They use actions, story maps, repeated phrases and oral rehearsal to help them remember and retell texts.
This gives children a strong foundation for writing because they have already practised the language, sequence and structure aloud.
Talk for Writing supports pupils to:
develop confidence as storytellers;
use richer vocabulary;
understand story structure;
rehearse sentences before writing;
move from spoken language into written composition.
As pupils become more confident, they are supported to change, adapt and create their own texts.
Writing
We view writing as a carefully taught, multi-step process.
Pupils are supported to develop their ideas, improve their accuracy and write for a range of audiences and purposes.
Our writing process includes:
Activating prior knowledgePupils revisit what they already know about the text type, vocabulary, grammar, content or core text before beginning new learning.
Explicit strategy instructionTeachers clearly explain the writing strategy, sentence structure or composition skill being taught.
Modelling of learned strategyTeachers model how to apply the strategy, making their thinking visible as they write.
Memorisation of strategyPupils practise key vocabulary, sentence stems, modelled phrases and structures so they can use them with increasing independence.
Oral rehearsalPupils say their ideas aloud, practise sentences and refine their language before writing.
Guided practicePupils practise with adult support through shared writing, partner work, sentence-level practice and feedback.
Independent practicePupils apply what they have learned in their own writing.
Structured reflectionPupils review their writing, consider the impact on the reader and identify how it could be improved.
This process helps pupils understand that writing is not simply about getting ideas onto a page.
It is about thinking, talking, rehearsing, drafting, improving and publishing.
The Writing Process
Our writing process includes:
PlanningGenerating ideas, identifying the purpose of writing and setting clear goals.
Oral rehearsalSaying sentences aloud, practising vocabulary and refining ideas before writing.
DraftingCapturing key ideas and developing content.
SharingReading work aloud and receiving feedback from adults and peers.
EvaluatingReflecting on whether writing goals have been met.
Revising and redraftingImproving content, structure, vocabulary, sentence control and impact.
EditingChecking accuracy, grammar, punctuation, spelling and coherence.
PublishingPresenting polished pieces of writing for others to read.
Teachers explicitly model writing so that pupils can see the thinking behind successful composition.
Grammar and sentence instruction are embedded within meaningful writing tasks so that pupils learn how to apply their skills in context.
Reading
Reading is at the heart of our curriculum.
We want every child to become a fluent, confident and thoughtful reader who enjoys books and can access the wider curriculum.
Our daily reading sessions help pupils develop fluency, vocabulary and comprehension.
Children are taught to understand the key reading domains by exploring:
what each reading skill means;
Teachers use guided oral reading, repeated reading and close reading to help pupils engage deeply with texts.
Adults model fluent reading, expression and phrasing, while pupils practise reading aloud and receive feedback.
Re-reading carefully chosen passages helps children build accuracy, automaticity, confidence and understanding.
Vocabulary Instruction
Vocabulary development is central to reading and writing success.
We explicitly teach important words and give pupils repeated opportunities to use them in speech and writing.
Our vocabulary teaching includes:
direct teaching of key Tier Two words;
exploring word meanings in context;
using dual coding to link words and images;
investigating synonyms, antonyms and word families;
practising new vocabulary through discussion, sentence work, chanting, cloze tasks and writing.

Maths at Nightingale
text
Maths teaching at Nightingale Primary is aimed at giving our children opportunities to develop and apply the goals set forth by the National Curriculum (NC). The three key aims of NC are to help children develop their fluency, problem-solving, and reasoning skills. To achieve these aims, a consistent approach founded in research is required.
Integrating Technology to Support Learning
We use evidence of best practices to support integrating digital platforms like IXL in our teaching. IXL plays a vital role in both guided and independent learning. The platform provides teachers immediate feedback as children progress through each question, allowing for real-time assessment and adjustments. Over the past year, our students have completed over 2 million questions on IXL, significantly enhancing their understanding and engagement during lessons.
Maths Mastery and more
Teachers work with senior leaders and the NCETM Maths Mastery Specialist to ensure consistent teaching quality. Alongside our Maths No Problem approach, we build opportunities for all children to stretch their mathematical thinking and mental arithmetic further. Across years 1 to 6, we have been introducing ‘Number Talks’, a focused approach to developing children’s mental arithmetic and confidence by applying a more comprehensive range of strategies.
We also use a range of tools and platforms to develop fluency with numbers, such as:
Times Tables Rockstars - encouraging engagement and regular practice of times tables
IXL - used effectively to target maths topics for homework and class lessons
Hit The Button - an online app/game that develops their times tables and number bonds
No Child Left Behind
We aim to have all our children make progress together and differentiate using a multitude of techniques, not by mathematical content. Whether our teachers use sharp questioning or move from concrete, pictorial and abstract, the aim is the same: no child is left behind. Over the past three years, 93% of our Year 6 pupils reached the national standard in Maths. We ensure all our children are exposed to complex and rich tasks within every concept through precisely selected activities to support them at their learning point.
Finding out more
If you have any questions regarding maths teaching at Nightingale or wish to visit one of our open mornings, please speak to Mr Rogerson, the maths lead, who will endeavour to help.

Life at Our School
text
From the moment you join Nightingale, you become part of a team that knows one another, supports one another and shares a commitment to helping children succeed.
As a small, one-form entry primary school, we are able to build strong relationships with our pupils, families and colleagues. There is a genuine sense of belonging here, with teamwork, kindness and mutual support shaping everyday school life. Many of our colleagues have chosen to spend much of their careers at Nightingale, creating a stable, experienced team that warmly welcomes new staff and enjoys working together.
No two days are ever the same. You might be inspiring children through engaging lessons, celebrating their achievements, supporting them to overcome challenges, working alongside families or contributing to the wider life of the school through community events, enrichment opportunities and whole-school initiatives.
Our commitment to children extends beyond the classroom. As a proud part of the Woolwich community, we work closely with families and local organisations, always striving to make a positive difference both inside and beyond the school gates. From our Eco-Schools work to being recognised as Superkind's Social Impact School of the Year, kindness, service and community spirit are woven into everyday life at Nightingale.

Opportunities to contribute to enrichment, sustainability and community initiatives
A positive working environment where wellbeing, respect and collaboration matter
